Claiming changes what buyers see. Once you edit your listing or mark it as checked, its page reads "Vendor maintained · Updated" with that date, where an unclaimed listing reads "AEC Integrations maintained". Buyers also see the links you add, such as the setup guide for an integration, and the details you keep current yourself.

AEC Integrations compiles its listings from public sources. A claim is how someone who works at a listed vendor asks for a seat on that vendor's account, so they can keep the listing accurate. Claiming is free, and you do not need an account to send one. We set up your account when we approve your claim.

## Send a claim

Choose **Claim your listing** on the [vendor program page](/vendor-program), search for your product or company, and pick it. Or open your company's page, or one of its product pages, and choose the claim button. It names your company, for example **Claim Acme Software**. A claim is also how you join your company's account when a colleague already has a seat.

If your product or company is not listed, use the [listing request form](/vendor-program/list-your-product), or choose **Not listed? Type it in** in the claim dialog. Give its name and website. We email you a link to confirm the request, the same way as a claim. Once you confirm it, we add the listing to the directory, then email you so you can finish your claim.

The form asks for:

- **Your name** and **Your role at the company**.
- **Your work email.** An address at your company's own domain helps us confirm you. We send the answer there, and it is the address you sign in with. If you enter a personal address, such as Gmail, Yahoo, AOL or Outlook.com, the form asks for your work email instead. You can still send the claim from a personal address, but confirming it may take longer.
- **LinkedIn profile (optional).** Adding it is the fastest way for us to confirm you work there.
- **Additional comments (optional)** A short note on your connection to the listing, up to 2,000 characters. Skip it if we asked you to claim.
- **I represent this company and accept the vendor terms.** You must tick this box to send a claim. It links to the [vendor terms](/legal/vendor-terms). We record the version you accepted, with the time you confirmed the claim.

Choose **Send claim**. We then email that address a link, and the form asks you to check your inbox. Your claim is not sent until you open the email, click **Confirm your claim**, and choose **Confirm and send** on the page it opens. The link works for 7 days and only once. If it does not arrive, check your spam folder, or send the claim again. If you got a link for a claim you did not send, ignore it: nothing happens unless someone clicks.

If you are signed in with the address you typed, we know it is yours, so there is no link. The claim goes straight in.

Once the claim is sent, the page confirms it, shows the address we will answer at, and lists what happens next. We also email that address a receipt that says what you claimed and what happens next. One address gets at most one receipt a day. Nothing changes on any account until a person approves a claim.

Each address can manage one company. If the address you typed already manages another company on AEC Integrations, or belongs to an AEC Integrations staff account, we can't accept the claim. When you confirm, the page tells you why, and we email you the same details. Send the claim again from a different work address.

If your company already has a team on AEC Integrations, the form tells you before you send. Your claim goes to that team first, and they confirm you. If they do not answer within 7 days, we step in and review it ourselves.

A claim on a product page is a claim on the vendor that makes the product. The seat you get covers the whole vendor account, not one product.

## What we check

A person at AEC Integrations reads every claim. Nothing is granted automatically. We look at:

- whether your email domain matches your company's website,
- your LinkedIn profile, or a search for your name if you left it blank,
- who already holds a seat on the account, and
- whether anyone else has claimed the same listing.

We do not use paid lookup services to check who you are. If we need more, we email you.

A person reviews every claim and emails you the result.

## What happens next

**If we approve it,** you get an email saying your claim is approved, with a button to your vendor portal. If you did not have an account, we create one for you. Sign in with the same address from the sign-in page. After that, open the portal from the account menu at the top right of any page, or go to [/vendor](/vendor). On a phone, the menu is at the top left. Approval puts every product on Free, and the email tells you what your account can do. To put a product on Managed, an owner buys a license on the **Billing** tab and assigns it. [Plans](/docs/vendors/plans) explains both plans. [Your seat](/docs/vendors/your-seat) covers what you can do from there.

**If we cannot approve it,** you get an email saying so. You are welcome to send a new claim with more detail about your role.

Once you have a seat, your company's requests and their status appear in the vendor portal under **Messages**. See [Notifications and messages](/docs/vendors/notifications-and-messages).

## If your company makes connector products

A connector product carries data between other products. If your company makes one, [For connector vendors](/docs/vendors/connector-vendors) covers the seat you can have and how we handle your claim.
